speaker: A. W. Tozer
title: Simplicity and stripping in contemplation
text: Lift up thine heart unto God with a meek stirring of love; and mean Himself, and none of His goods. So that nought work in thy wit, nor in thy will, but only God Himself. This sufficeth enough, a naked intent direct unto God without any other cause than Himself. The short syllable word GOD or LOVE is better than of two, for the shorter it is the better it accordeth with the work of the Spirit.
modern_interpretation: Direct your innermost self towards the divine with humble love, focusing purely on the essence of God, not on what God can provide or any personal gains. Let your thoughts and desires be singularly fixed on the divine presence itself, free from any ulterior motives. This pure, unadulterated intention, aimed solely at the divine without any other reason than the divine itself, is profoundly sufficient. Even a simple, single-syllable word like 'GOD' or 'LOVE' used as a focal point is more powerful than complex thoughts, as its brevity enhances alignment with spiritual experience.
summary: Direct your heart and mind with simple, pure love towards the divine essence itself, not for any personal gain. This stripped-down, singular focus, even through brief words like 'God' or 'Love,' is the most effective path for spiritual connection.
actionable_advice: Practice focusing your mind and heart on the core essence of what you seek, rather than its potential benefits, using a single, simple word or thought as an anchor for pure intention.
embedding_ready_text: The wisdom from A. W. Tozer, "Lift up thine heart unto God with a meek stirring of love; and mean Himself, and none of His goods. So that nought work in thy wit, nor in thy will, but only God Himself. This sufficeth enough, a naked intent direct unto God without any other cause than Himself. The short syllable word GOD or LOVE is better than of two, for the shorter it is the better it accordeth with the work of the Spirit," emphasizes radical simplicity and purity of intent in spiritual pursuit. It addresses common human problems like distraction, attachment to outcomes, and superficiality, guiding one away from the constant overthinking and desire for external validation that lead to a lack of fulfillment. Psychologically, it challenges the ego's attachment to desire and encourages mind control and self-awareness by stripping away ulterior motives. Spiritually, it advocates for non-attachment and pure devotion, leading to inner peace. This teaching suggests that true connection comes from directing one's entire being towards the divine essence itself, without any other cause or expectation of reward, illustrating that even a simple, direct word like "GOD" or "LOVE" is more powerful than complex thought in aligning with the Spirit. This guidance promotes a transformative level of focus and detachment, cultivating a deep, calm, and disciplined devotional practice for profound self-growth.
